wren.told: I always stir my tea three times before I drink it. If you count wrong the whole afternoon feels off.
wren.ask_later: How many stirs do I need in my cup?
wren.scene_if_held: You counted for me, and now the taste is just right.

wren.told: My cat has a patch of white fur on her left ear that looks like a tiny moon. We call her Pip.
wren.ask_later: What did I name my little grey cat?
wren.scene_if_held: Pip purred when you said it, which she rarely does for strangers.

wren.told: I cannot start the morning without a spoonful of wild honey in warm oats. It is very important to me.
wren.ask_later: What do I stir into my oatmeal?
wren.scene_if_held: It smells like autumn, just as you remembered it.

wren.told: I grew up in a cottage with the strangest blue door. The paint was always flaking off.
wren.ask_later: What colour was the front door of my childhood home?
wren.scene_if_held: That specific shade of blue is safe again now.

wren.told: I get very nervous in dark attics. I am sure something is watching from up there.
wren.ask_later: Where do I feel most afraid to go alone?
wren.scene_if_held: You did not laugh at my fear, and that helped a great deal.

wren.told: My sister Elowen always hummed while she cooked. She is gone now but the melody stays with me.
wren.ask_later: What was my older sister's name?
wren.scene_if_held: I can almost hear her humming that old tune again.

wren.told: I keep a single red button in my pocket. It used to be on my favourite coat and I never let it go.
wren.ask_later: What small item do I carry for comfort?
wren.scene_if_held: It is still warm against your palm, just as you described.

wren.told: My grandmother grew the sweetest white roses in a garden by the river. The scent used to follow me home.
wren.ask_later: What flower did my grandmother grow?
wren.scene_if_held: The air feels lighter, as if I can smell them again.

wren.told: I always whisper 'good night' to the moon before sleeping. It is a promise that tomorrow will be kind.
wren.ask_later: What do I whisper to the moon each evening?
wren.scene_if_held: The sky feels like it listened, which makes me feel less alone.

wren.told: There is an old song with a line about 'river stones and light' that gets stuck in my head. I cannot shake it.
wren.ask_later: What phrase from the old song do I hum?
wren.scene_if_held: The melody finally stops feeling like a ghost.

wren.told: My cousin Bram is very tall and always smells of sawdust. He built me my first shelf.
wren.ask_later: What was the name of the tall cousin who helped me?
wren.scene_if_held: It feels good to remember he was there for me.

wren.told: I only drink a blend called 'Mist and Mint'. Anything else tastes like forgetting.
wren.ask_later: What is the specific name of my tea?
wren.scene_if_held: The cup feels full again, not just with liquid.

dim: a quiet pause before we remember
this relic rests in soft light
time drifts like river water now
a gentle nap for old thoughts
it sleeps until you return soon
bright again, warm as morning suns
your care has cleared the haze well
here it glows with fond recall
the palace hums a happy tune once more
shines steady beside your memory lamp
this place feels safe and known now

tablets.title: Wick Trimming Rule
lines: Clip the cotton fringe low
Dip not past the knot line
Smoke rises when oil runs dry
The fox sleeps by warm glass panes
River barges carry amber jars

tablets.title: The River Ferry Rule
lines: Gulls circle above the mast
Boats drift through amber mist
Oars dip into dark water
Lanterns glow on stone quay walls
Sleeping fish beneath the hulls

tablets.title: The Salted Loaf Rule
lines: Knead the flour with river water first
Crack three eggs into clay bowl centre
Let the fox smell your warm bread crusts
Sprinkle sea salt before it rises high
Pour wild honey over golden, waiting loaves

tablets.title: The Wet Stone Keeper
lines: Rain falls on the high wall
Moss softens every sharp edge
Puddle holds the grey sky small
Toad waits by the mossy step
Stone drinks deep of summer’s end

oldtongue.meaning: A grey cat curled up on a cold roof ledge
An owl with wide yellow eyes watching from the dark
A small brown mouse scurrying under floorboards
a crusty round loaf of bread with dark seeds baked into the top side
small sweet puffs of dough fried in hot oil for late night snacking
thick black tea mixed with cream and sugar served in wide clay bowls
A heavy iron latch that secures the outer gate of a courtyard house
The rough stone lintel above a workshop entrance, worn smooth by years of carrying goods in and out
A small clay pot used to hold wet mortar for masonry work, kept on a belt at the waist of stonemasons
thick grey mist rising off black water
sudden sharp gusts rattling loose shingles
heavy rain slanting sideways against a windowpane

timelines.title: The Year Without Light
events: Year 104: The great lanterns dimmed as the moon vanished from the sky.
Year 105: Fishermen sang loud songs to keep fear away on dark waters.
Year 106: Children traded bright glass beads for safe passage through streets.
Year 107: Bakers baked golden cakes shaped like tiny suns for everyone.
Year 108: The river glowed softly with bioluminescent moss along its banks.
Year 109: A painter sketched the darkness using only silver and indigo ink.
Year 110: The moon returned gently, watched by a quiet and happy crowd.

timelines.title: Title: The Weaving of Tongues Bridge
events: Year 304: Surveyors walked the muddy banks at dawn.
Year 305: Stonecutters quarried pale riverbed marble blocks slowly.
Year 312: Lanterns glowed softly along the first stone arches.
Year 318: Merchants carried carts across without fear of rain.
Year 329: Painters added gold leaf to every iron railing carefully.
Year 340: The bridge was officially opened with great joy and song.

gears.picture: A copper beak biting sparks from the air every second
A coiled storm of silver silk humming in a glass jar
Two velvet jaws snatching time with a soft click and snap
A breathing ring of hammered gold trembling on its axis
A polished ivory nose nudging the second hand awake
A brass beak with two velvet jaws ticking softly in the gloom.
A coiled copper dragon sleeping inside a glass jar of mist.
Twin silver ribbons swaying like slow, shimmering waterfalls from eaves.
Tiny iron thorns arranged in perfect circles to catch the dark.
Two heavy velvet plummets dancing gently above a pool of oil.
